what_its_for: Nepafenac is an anti-inflammatory eye drop used to treat pain and swelling in your eye after cataract surgery. It belongs to a group of medicines called NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) that help reduce inflammation in the eye.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using. Shake the bottle well before each use. Tilt your head back, pull your lower eyelid down gently to form a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink or squeeze your eye tightly. Press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger to prevent the medicine from draining away. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, eyelid, or any surface to avoid contamination. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each one.
dosing: For Nevanac (0.1% suspension): Use 1 drop in the affected eye 3 times a day, starting 1 day before your cataract surgery, continuing on the day of surgery, and for 2 weeks after surgery. For Ilevro (0.3% suspension): Use 1 drop in the affected eye once daily, starting 1 day before surgery, continuing on the day of surgery, and for 2 weeks after surgery, then 1 additional drop 30 to 120 minutes before surgery. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may differ.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine and all medicines out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear contact lenses while using nepafenac eye drops, especially if your eye is red or irritated. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface, your eye, or fingers to prevent contamination. Do not use the drops if you are allergic to aspirin, ibuprofen, or other NSAIDs without first checking with your doctor. Avoid driving or operating machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: increased eye pain, redness, or swelling; sudden changes in your vision or vision loss; eye discharge or crusting; signs of an eye infection; a feeling that something is in your eye that does not go away; blistering or peeling around the eye; or if your symptoms do not improve or get worse. Seek emergency care if you experience sudden vision loss.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some relief from eye pain and discomfort within a day or two of starting nepafenac. However, it is important to keep using the drops for the full time prescribed by your doctor, even if your eye feels better, to make sure the inflammation is fully controlled after surgery.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding patients: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Nepafenac should be avoided starting at 20 weeks of pregnancy and is not recommended after 30 weeks. Ask your doctor before using if you are breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 10 years old has not been established. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but they should be monitored carefully. Patients with bleeding problems: Use with caution if you have a bleeding disorder or are taking blood thinners, as eye drops may slightly affect clotting in the eye area.
